newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen bull run seen straddling HK handover.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen bull run seen straddling HK handover.

text.p: Shenzhen B shares are likely to surge further to historic highs in the lead up to the Hong Kong handover as investors doubt the possibility of another market clampdown, analysts said on Wednesday.

"General euphoria in China over the Hong Kong handover will help the Shenzhen B share index surge to 250 points," an analyst at China Guotai Securities told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin on Wednesday.
The foreign currency B index closed on Wednesday at 177.09 after hitting a 1997 high of 181.79 points on Monday.
The all-time high of 201.87 was touched in mid-December just before stock prices crashed 30 percent following an official warning from Beijing on market speculation and overheating.
Prices on both the Shenzhen and Shanghai exchanges have been rising steadily since January on the back of fundamental optimism about the economy and the results of listed firms.
Shenzhen B share prices are expected to shoot past last December's high by June, brokers said, as Hong Kong's reversion to Chinese control keeps sentiment positive.
"The handover, along with the Shenzhen government's plans to boost the B share market, will continue to fuel the strong upward momentum," an analyst at J&A Securities said.
The British colony of Hong Kong, next door to Shenzhen, will be returned to China at midnight on June 30, 1997.
Analysts said the Chinese government was unlikely to crack down on the securities market unless it became seriously overheated because Beijing wants a smooth and positive Hong Kong handover.
"The government will not want to see a crash during the handover when the world is watching," an analyst at a Hong Kong investment bank in Shenzhen said.
The Shenzhen market and the city's government are also taking steps to keep their stock exchange buoyant.
A recent newspaper report said Shenzhen was planning to set up a new stock data network in Hong Kong to improve the flow of information about B shares to investors.
The Shenzhen securities authorities are encouraging B share promotional tours abroad to boost the market, the Shenzhen-based Securities Times quoted a senior city official as saying.
Few people predict a repeat of December's official efforts to cool the market down.
"The December crackdown angered many market players and I doubt the government would want to do this again so soon," the Hong Kong investment bank analyst said.
